title: The Ledger of Saint Alder's
premise: Estate lawyer Odile Brightwater is hired by a dying stranger, Marlowe Vane, to prove that a murder recorded in the ancient ledger of Saint Alder's parish has not yet happened — because the victim is Odile herself, and the date is three weeks away. Following a trail of coded entries hidden in plain sight among wills, baptisms, and burial records, Odile uncovers a centuries-old covenant: each generation, the ledger's keepers must 'balance' it with a death, and her own name was entered at birth. As she races the ledger's prophecy, she discovers the killer is someone bound to her by love rather than duty — and in the end she breaks the covenant not by escaping the murder, but by proving the ledger only holds power over those who believe their names are written, freeing Saint Alder's village from its inherited debt.
about_author: Freya Nakamura is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing parish records in coastal England before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries where documents lie, families are chosen, and every locked drawer hides a heart.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Odile Brightwater, meticulous and emotionally walled-off, takes an unusual retainer from the frail Marlowe Vane: prove that a murder listed in Saint Alder's ledger hasn't happened yet. The victim's name is her own. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: unease masked as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: At Saint Alder's parish archive, Odile finds Vane's own will already filed — dated for his death next month — though he is alive and insists he wrote no such thing. The ledger's margin bears her name in faded ink. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the first crack in her rational worldview.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Cottage
chapters.summary: Odile meets Wren Halloway, the young, prickly keeper of the ledger who inherited the post from a grandmother she barely knew. Wren warns her away; Odile refuses. Their friction sparks something like recognition. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance against shared dread.

chapters.title: Baptisms, Burials, Balances
chapters.summary: Decoding the ledger's structure, Odile finds every generation ends with one 'balancing' death — always a Brightwater or a Halloway. Her mother's name appears forty years ago, unexplained. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as motive.

chapters.title: What the Village Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile canvasses Saint Alder's locals, meeting innkeeper Tobias Finch, whose warmth disarms her. Everyone speaks of the ledger with fond reverence — and quiet fear. Someone follows her back to the cottage. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: isolation beginning to thaw into belonging.

chapters.title: Marlowe's Confession
chapters.summary: Vane admits he hired her not to prevent her murder but to witness it: he is the current debtor, dying anyway, and the ledger demands a substitute. He claims he chose her out of mercy. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Shifting to Wren's POV, we learn she has known Odile's name was in the ledger since childhood — and that her grandmother trained her to protect the covenant, not question it. Wren's loyalty splits. Emotional beat: duty versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Odile discovers the ledger's true entries hide beneath devotional verses — a cipher mapping debts across generations. One entry, dated three weeks hence, reads simply: 'O.B., paid in full.' POV: Odile. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: Tobias's Kindness
chapters.summary: A storm strands Odile at the inn; Tobias shares his own loss — a sister whose name once appeared in the ledger. He believes, and his belief frightens her more than doubt would. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: tenderness entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Odile finds a second forged document — her own death certificate, pre-signed by a doctor long dead. Someone inside the parish machinery is preparing the paperwork of her murder. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Halloway Secrets
chapters.summary: In Wren's POV, she confronts her grandmother's journals and learns the covenant was invented two generations ago to cover a real crime — a Halloway killed a Brightwater, and the ledger became the alibi. Emotional beat: horror at inherited guilt.

chapters.title: An Offer of Escape
chapters.summary: Vane offers Odile a way out: leave Saint Alder's forever and let the debt pass to another Brightwater descendant — a child in the village registry. Her refusal costs her his protection. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: love against duty, first tested.

chapters.title: The Night Watch
chapters.summary: Odile and Wren stake out the crypt where the ledger's 'payments' were historically made. They catch a figure burning documents — Tobias, destroying evidence of his sister's entry. Trust fractures. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: betrayal of the heart.

chapters.title: What Tobias Burned
chapters.summary: The burned pages, partially recovered, reveal Tobias's sister didn't die of the covenant — she was murdered by the last keeper, Wren's grandmother, to settle a private grudge. The covenant is a weapon wearing tradition's face. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Vane dies peacefully in his sleep — but the ledger marks his death as 'unbalanced,' meaning the debt now falls due immediately, on Odile, within days. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: clock running out.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren, in her POV, must decide: perform the ritual that legitimizes the killing, or destroy the ledger and inherit her grandmother's crime publicly. She chooses to help Odile forge a counter-entry. Emotional beat: found family sealed in complicity.

chapters.title: The Counter-Entry
chapters.summary: Working through the night, Odile and Wren write a false balancing payment into the cipher — naming the original murderer, dead forty years, as the debt paid. But the forgery requires a keeper's seal, which means confessing everything to the parish council. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: courage as exposure.

chapters.title: Council of Saint Alder's
chapters.summary: Before the council, Odile lays bare the covenant's fraudulent history. Half the village recoils; half, led by Tobias, stands with her. The council's eldest reveals he has been maintaining the fraud for decades. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: truth as weapon and wound.

chapters.title: The True Debtor
chapters.summary: The eldest councillor — the doctor's son who forged her death certificate — attempts to complete the killing himself, believing the ledger's power rests on completion. He corners Odile in the crypt. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: climax of fear.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Wren arrives and, before witnesses, strikes the final entry from the ledger with the keeper's own pen — declaring the account closed. The elder collapses not from violence but from the collapse of the belief that sustained him. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the spell broken.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Odile probates Vane's real will: he left everything to fund the archive's honest keeping, naming both Odile and Wren as trustees. The village begins rewriting its records truthfully. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile stays in Saint Alder's, opening a small practice above the inn. On the first blank page of a new book, Wren writes two names side by side — not debts, but a promise. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: home, chosen freely.
